title: Periodic Table at Three Resolutions
claim: The Consilience Atlas uses one invariant Periodic-15 grammar at Local, Series, and Global resolutions; higher resolutions aggregate the same meanings rather than inventing a new classification language, while cross-series Phi remains a comparison operation rather than a storage resolution.
assumptions: Primitive semantic objects and typed edges are stored canonically before projection.
Aggregation rules must be declared rather than inferred from visual similarity.
Candidate and Admitted graph states remain distinct at every resolution.
definitions: Local: atom/object-level Periodic-15 plus dependency, warrant, dynamics, orientation, bridges, Reality Mirror, and receipts.
Series: the same Periodic-15 grammar aggregated over papers/atoms with longitudinal resolution, invariant, bridge-family, anchor, and bottleneck views.
Global: the same Periodic-15 grammar aggregated over series plus Phi registry, anomaly register, emergent topology, global blast radius, external-anchor coverage, and convergence/divergence views.
Phi Cross-Series: a comparison operation between Series records; not a fourth storage resolution.
negative_guards: Do not add a new marker merely because a higher-resolution view is more complex.
Do not treat map membership as a new semantic classification when it is derivable from canonical objects/edges.
Do not let aggregate standing or evidence grade inherit automatically from child records.
kill_conditions: A required Local/Series/Global object cannot be represented without changing the meaning/order of the Periodic-15 markers and cannot be represented as metadata, typed edge, registry object, or computed projection.
The same marker acquires incompatible semantics at different stored resolutions.

ledger.meaning: Registered the invariant Periodic-15 grammar across Local, Series, and Global resolution.
ledger.limits: Registration is an architecture receipt, not proof that every corpus will fit without amendment.
